title: HbA1c Trend Analysis for Mrs. Asha Kunwar Rathod
keyFindings: HbA1c levels consistently above the diabetic threshold (>6.5%) in all three reports.
Estimated average glucose (eAg) values are elevated and rising: 159.1 mg/dL, 164.8 mg/dL, and 180.0 mg/dL.
HbA1c control has shifted from fair to approaching poor as per ADA guidelines.
No evidence of improvement in glycemic control over the course of the year.
All results are flagged as abnormal, indicating suboptimal diabetes management.
summary: This document summarizes three sequential HbA1c laboratory reports for Mrs. Asha Kunwar Rathod, a 36-year-old female patient under the care of Dr. V. N. Shah at Zydus Hospital. The reports, dated March 2024, May 2024, and January 2025, show a consistent and progressive elevation in HbA1c levels: 7.17%, 7.37%, and 7.9%, respectively. These values are well above the diagnostic threshold for diabetes (>6.5%) and indicate a transition from fair to nearly poor glycemic control according to ADA recommendations. Correspondingly, the estimated average glucose (eAg) values have also increased over time, from 159.1 mg/dL to 180.0 mg/dL, further confirming deteriorating blood sugar control. All results are highlighted as abnormal, and there is no evidence of improvement in diabetes management over the observed period. These findings suggest a need for urgent review and intensification of the patient's diabetes care plan to prevent potential complications.
recommendations: Review and intensify the current diabetes management plan, including possible medication adjustments.
Consult with a diabetologist or endocrinologist for specialized guidance.
Implement or reinforce lifestyle modifications, such as dietary changes and increased physical activity.
Schedule more frequent monitoring of HbA1c and blood glucose levels to assess response to interventions.
Educate the patient on the importance of adherence to therapy and regular follow-up visits.
